title: Consuming External HTTP Services
subtopics: Making server-side HTTP requests with suitable COM components
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of consuming external http services in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Understanding API endpoints and HTTP methods and status codes.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study consuming external http services as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 84 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Consuming External HTTP Services matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP often relies on Windows COM components and external services for file operations, messaging, XML, and integration. For 'Consuming External HTTP Services', document the exact component/provider version, permissions, bitness, network boundaries, timeouts, and recovery behavior. Never construct a filesystem path or external URL directly from untrusted input, and keep secrets outside the public web root and repository.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Understanding API endpoints; HTTP methods and status codes; Making server-side HTTP requests with suitable COM components; Setting headers; Handling timeouts and network errors; Parsing JSON or XML responses; API credentials and service authentication. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Consuming External HTTP Services
content_blocks.code:
<%
Dim http
Set http = Server.CreateObject("MSXML2.ServerXMLHTTP.6.0")
http.setTimeouts 3000, 3000, 5000, 5000
' Use a fixed, approved HTTPS endpoint; do not take arbitrary URLs from Request.
' http.Open "GET", "https://api.example.test/status", False
' http.Send
' Check http.Status and validate the response body before use.
Set http = Nothing
%>

content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a host allow-list, enforce TLS validation, handle non-2xx responses/malformed bodies, and avoid forwarding secrets to third-party services. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use approved test data and a component/service you control. Confirm path permissions, host allow-lists, timeouts, malformed responses, and cleanup behavior. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of consuming external http services. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of consuming external http services using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Understanding API endpoints. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
